docs.title: MONET Plots
docs.text: A comprehensive plotting library for scientific visualization, spun off from the main MONET repository. MONET Plots provides a modular, extensible framework for creating high-quality scientific plots with a focus on meteorological and climate data visualization.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: MONET Plots is designed to make scientific plotting easier, more consistent, and publication-ready. It leverages the power of Matplotlib and Cartopy while providing a simplified API and consistent styling.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Modular Plot Classes: Extensible plot classes for common scientific visualization needs
  • Publication-Ready Styling: Built-in Wiley-compliant styling for professional appearance
  • Cartopy Integration: Seamless integration with cartopy for geospatial plotting
  • Multiple Plot Types: Spatial, time series, scatter, Taylor diagrams, KDE plots, and more
  • Flexible Configuration: Easy customization of colors, styles, and plot parameters
  • Performance Optimized: Designed for efficient plotting with large datasets

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or higher
  • pip package manager

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text: pip install monet_plots

docs.title: Install from Source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/your-repo/monet-plots.git
cd monet-plots
pip install -e .

docs.title: Install Optional Dependencies
docs.text:
For full functionality, install additional optional dependencies:

# For geospatial plotting
pip install cartopy

# For statistical plotting
pip install pandas

# For advanced Taylor diagrams
pip install numpy matplotlib

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from monet_plots import SpatialPlot, TimeSeriesPlot, ScatterPlot

# Create sample data
lat = np.linspace(30, 50, 20)
lon = np.linspace(-120, -70, 30)
data = np.random.random((20, 30))

# Create a spatial plot
spatial_plot = SpatialPlot()
spatial_plot.plot(data, title="Sample Spatial Plot")
spatial_plot.save("spatial_plot.png")

# Create time series data
dates = pd.date_range('2023-01-01', periods=100, freq='D')
time_series_data = pd.DataFrame({
    'time': dates,
    'obs': np.random.normal(0, 1, 100) + np.sin(np.arange(100) * 0.1)
})

# Create a time series plot
ts_plot = TimeSeriesPlot()
ts_plot.plot(time_series_data, x='time', y='obs', title="Time Series Example")
ts_plot.save("timeseries_plot.png")

docs.title: Getting Started Guide
docs.text: Welcome to MONET Plots! This comprehensive guide will help you get up and running quickly with our scientific plotting library, from installation to creating your first professional plots.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Python: 3.11 or higher (CI covers 3.11–3.14)
  • pip: Python package manager (comes with Python)
  • Optional: conda (for managing complex dependencies)
  • Memory: Minimum 512MB RAM (1GB+ recommended for large datasets)
  • Disk: 50MB free space for installation

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before installing MONET Plots, ensure you have the following:

# Check Python version
python --version  # Should be 3.7 or higher

# Check pip is installed and working
pip --version

# Update pip to latest version
python -m pip install --upgrade pip

docs.title: 1. Install MONET Plots
docs.text:
# Install the latest stable release from PyPI
pip install monet_plots

# For the latest development version
pip install git+https://github.com/your-repo/monet-plots.git

# Install specific version (if needed)
pip install monet_plots==1.0.0

docs.title: 2. Install Optional Dependencies
docs.text:
MONET Plots has a modular design with optional dependencies for enhanced functionality. Install these based on your needs:

Core Dependencies (Recommended for most users): 

# Essential data processing and visualization
pip install pandas matplotlib

# Statistical computing
pip install numpy scipy

Geospatial and Climate Data: 

# For geographical maps and projections
pip install cartopy

# For NetCDF file handling
pip install xarray netcdf4

# For advanced geospatial operations
pip install shapely pyproj

Advanced Statistical Features: 

# For machine learning integration
pip install scikit-learn

# For advanced statistical analysis
pip install statsmodels

Development and Testing: 

# For development
pip install pytest black isort mypy

# Documentation generation
pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material

docs.title: 3. Verify Installation
docs.text:
Test your installation with these verification steps:

# Basic import test
import monet_plots
print(f"MONET Plots version: {monet_plots.__version__}")

# Test all major components
try:
    from monet_plots import (
        SpatialPlot, TimeSeriesPlot, ScatterPlot,
        TaylorDiagramPlot, KDEPlot, WindQuiverPlot, WindBarbsPlot,
        FacetGridPlot
    )
    print("All plot classes imported successfully!")
except ImportError as e:
    print(f"Import error: {e}")

# Test optional dependencies
try:
    import cartopy
    print("Cartopy available for geospatial plotting")
except ImportError:
    print("Cartopy not available - install for geospatial features")

try:
    import xarray
    print("xarray available for NetCDF support")
except ImportError:
    print("xarray not available - install for NetCDF support")

You should see success messages for all components without any errors.

docs.title: Your First Plot
docs.text:
Let's create a simple time series plot to demonstrate the basic workflow:

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from monet_plots import TimeSeriesPlot

# Create sample data
dates = pd.date_range('2023-01-01', periods=100, freq='D')
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'time': dates,
    'temperature': 20 + 10 * np.sin(np.arange(100) * 0.1) + np.random.normal(0, 2, 100)
})

# Create and plot
plot = TimeSeriesPlot()
plot.plot(data, x='time', y='temperature', title='Daily Temperature', ylabel='Temperature (°C)')
plot.save('temperature_plot.png')
plot.close()

docs.title: Plot Classes
docs.text:
MONET Plots follows a class-based architecture where each plot type has its own class:

BasePlot (abstract base class)
├── SpatialPlot
├── TimeSeriesPlot
├── TimeSeriesPlot
├── ScatterPlot
├── TaylorDiagramPlot
├── KDEPlot
├── WindQuiverPlot
└── WindBarbsPlot

docs.title: Common Workflow
docs.text:
1. Initialize: Create a plot instance with desired parameters
  2. Plot: Call the plot method with your data
  3. Customize: Add labels, titles, and other customizations
  4. Save: Export the plot to file
  5. Close: Close the plot to free memory
# General workflow pattern
plot = SpatialPlot(figsize=(10, 6))         # 1. Initialize
plot.plot(data, cmap='viridis')             # 2. Plot data
plot.title("My Plot").xlabel("X Axis")      # 3. Customize
plot.save("output.png")                    # 4. Save
plot.close()                               # 5. Close

docs.title: Observation, model and bias maps
docs.text:
compare_spatial creates three columns: observations, model values, and model minus observations. Observations and model values share one scale; bias uses a separate diverging scale centered on zero. Add row="model" or row="season" for repeated comparisons.

import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import monet_plots as mp

# DataArrays already collocated on the same grid, in the same physical units.
# observations: lat × lon; predictions: model × lat × lon.
result = mp.compare_spatial(
    observations, predictions,
    row="model",
    projection=ccrs.LambertConformal(),
    extent=(-125, -65, 24, 51),
    vmin=0, vmax=60, bias_limit=8,
    cmap="viridis", bias_cmap="RdBu_r",
    rasterized=True,
)
result.save("model-evaluation.pdf")

The runnable example uses synthetic surface ozone and a missing observation region. It needs no scientific data download; Cartopy caches the coastline on first use.

docs.title: Pairing and interpretation
docs.text:
Inputs are xarray DataArrays. Select Dataset variables explicitly. Field dimension names, sizes, index labels, and spatial coordinates must match exactly. For curvilinear grids, the 2D longitude and latitude coordinates must also match. Where dimensions lack explicit index labels, they pair by position; the spatial coordinates must still match. Supply explicit period/model labels to make those comparisons unambiguous. Only a model-only row dimension broadcasts static observations intentionally. Use kind="scatter" for collocated station pairs on a shared sample dimension.

Model output and station observations must be collocated before calling this function. Regrid/interpolate explicitly, choose a scientifically justified method, and align averaging windows and vertical levels. This function does not infer representativeness, collocation, unit conversion, or statistical significance.

Both inputs must have the same units attribute, or both must omit it. Supplying units on only one input raises an error. Unit strings are compared literally: convert equivalent units and normalize their labels beforehand. data_crs applies to both inputs; projected coordinates require an explicit CRS.

Non-finite values remain masked. A bias is shown only where both inputs are finite. The observation/model panels retain their individual valid values, even where a pair is missing. The returned bias, paired, and paired_counts expose those choices as xarray objects; counts are per row and have dimensionless units. Differences are calculated as model − observations, never the reverse.

docs.title: Scales and performance
docs.text:
vmin and vmax set the common observation/model bounds. bias_limit=8 sets bias bounds to −8 and +8. Without limits, the common bounds cover finite values from both inputs and bias limits use the largest absolute finite paired difference across all rows. All-zero bias uses ±1 to retain a valid zero-centered scale.

A custom concentration norm is supported. For bias, a custom bias_norm must be a TwoSlopeNorm centered on zero; do not combine it with bias_limit. Use cbar_kwargs for shared colorbar options and bias_cbar_kwargs to override bias-specific options. Set colorbar=False to omit both bars.

Automatic bounds are reduced in one shared Dask compute graph. Explicit bounds skip those reductions. By default, materialize="row" evaluates the three fields in one shared graph per row, avoiding repeated source work without persisting an entire cube. materialize="panel" evaluates panels independently for comparison or different memory tradeoffs. Temporary arrays and Matplotlib artists still consume memory; reducing the number of tasks does not guarantee lower peak RSS.

SpatialComparisonPlot(...).plot() offers the same workflow with delayed rendering. Construction preserves lazy field values and checks coordinates; validation may evaluate lazy coordinate arrays. The object can be rendered once; create a new object for another configuration.

print(result.paired_counts.compute())
# Inspect bias directly with xarray:
print(result.bias.mean().compute())

Do not use unweighted spatial means for quantitative conclusions when grid-cell areas or sampling weights differ. Aggregation and weighting remain explicit analysis steps.

Bases: BasePlot

Observation, model and model-minus-observation panels, optionally by row.

Inputs must be xarray DataArrays with the same dimension labels and spatial coordinates, already in the same units and CRS. A model-only row dimension intentionally repeats static observations for each model/period. All other broadcasting and implicit regridding are rejected. Initialization preserves lazy field values; rendering resolves scales and computes panels.

Source code in src/monet_plots/plots/spatial_comparison.py 
class SpatialComparisonPlot(BasePlot):
    """Observation, model and model-minus-observation panels, optionally by row.

    Inputs must be xarray DataArrays with the same dimension labels and spatial
    coordinates, already in the same units and CRS. A model-only ``row``
    dimension intentionally repeats static observations for each model/period.
    All other broadcasting and implicit regridding are rejected. Initialization
    preserves lazy field values; rendering resolves scales and computes panels.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        observations,
        model,
        *,
        row=None,
        kind="pcolormesh",
        x=None,
        y=None,
        projection=None,
        data_crs=None,
        extent_crs=None,
        size=3,
        aspect=1.25,
        style="wiley",
        **kwargs,
    ):
        if not isinstance(observations, xr.DataArray) or not isinstance(
            model, xr.DataArray
        ):
            raise TypeError(
                "Comparison inputs must be xarray DataArrays; select Dataset variables explicitly."
            )
        if kind not in {"pcolormesh", "imshow", "contourf", "scatter"}:
            raise ValueError("kind must be pcolormesh, imshow, contourf, or scatter.")
        self.x, self.y = identify_coords(model, x, y)
        self.observations, self.model = _paired_fields(
            observations,
            model,
            row=row,
            x=self.x,
            y=self.y,
        )
        validate_data_crs(model, self.x, self.y, data_crs)
        validate_data_crs(observations, self.x, self.y, data_crs)
        self.row, self.kind = row, kind
        field_dims = [dim for dim in model.dims if dim != row]
        expected = 1 if kind == "scatter" else 2
        if len(field_dims) != expected:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{kind} requires {expected} field dimensions; select extra dimensions or specify row."
            )
        self.paired = np.isfinite(self.model) & np.isfinite(self.observations)
        self.bias = (self.model - self.observations).where(self.paired)
        self.bias.name = "bias"
        self.bias.attrs = {"long_name": "Model − observations"}
        if model.attrs.get("units"):
            self.bias.attrs["units"] = model.attrs["units"]
        self.paired_counts = self.paired.sum(dim=field_dims)
        self.paired_counts.attrs = {
            "long_name": "Finite observation/model pairs",
            "units": "1",
        }
        self.data_crs = data_crs or ccrs.PlateCarree()
        self.extent_crs = extent_crs or ccrs.PlateCarree()
        self.render_options = kwargs
        self.plotters, self.mappables = [], []
        rows = model.sizes[row] if row else 1
        if rows == 0:
            raise ValueError("The comparison needs at least one row.")
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(
            rows,
            3,
            squeeze=False,
            figsize=(3 * size * aspect, rows * size),
            subplot_kw={"projection": projection or ccrs.PlateCarree()},
            layout="constrained",
        )
        super().__init__(fig=fig, ax=axes[0, 0], style=style)
        self.axes = axes

    def plot(
        self,
        *,
        vmin=None,
        vmax=None,
        norm=None,
        bias_limit=None,
        bias_norm=None,
        cmap="viridis",
        bias_cmap="RdBu_r",
        colorbar=True,
        cbar_kwargs=None,
        bias_cbar_kwargs=None,
        panel_labels=True,
        materialize="row",
        **kwargs,
    ):
        """Render with a common concentration scale and a zero-centered bias scale.

        Explicit vmin/vmax and bias_limit avoid global scale reductions. With
        automatic limits, all required scalar reductions share one Dask compute
        call. ``bias_norm`` must be a TwoSlopeNorm centered on zero; explicit
        ``bias_limit`` uses symmetric bounds. Empty panels retain masked values.
        """
        if self.mappables:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "This comparison has already been rendered; create a new plot to render again."
            )
        options = {**self.render_options, **kwargs}
        # Accept rendering configuration through the convenience constructor too.
        vmin, vmax = options.pop("vmin", vmin), options.pop("vmax", vmax)
        norm = options.pop("norm", norm)
        bias_limit = options.pop("bias_limit", bias_limit)
        bias_norm = options.pop("bias_norm", bias_norm)
        cmap, bias_cmap = options.pop("cmap", cmap), options.pop("bias_cmap", bias_cmap)
        colorbar = options.pop("colorbar", colorbar)
        cbar_kwargs = options.pop("cbar_kwargs", cbar_kwargs) or {}
        bias_cbar_kwargs = options.pop("bias_cbar_kwargs", bias_cbar_kwargs) or {}
        panel_labels = options.pop("panel_labels", panel_labels)
        materialize = options.pop("materialize", materialize)
        if materialize not in {"row", "panel"}:
            raise ValueError("materialize must be row or panel.")
        self.field_norm, self.bias_norm = _comparison_norms(
            self.observations,
            self.model,
            self.bias,
            vmin=vmin,
            vmax=vmax,
            norm=norm,
            bias_limit=bias_limit,
            bias_norm=bias_norm,
        )
        renderers = {
            "pcolormesh": SpatialMeshPlot,
            "imshow": SpatialImshowPlot,
            "contourf": SpatialContourPlot,
            "scatter": SpatialTrack,
        }
        feature_keys = {
            "extent",
            "coastlines",
            "states",
            "countries",
            "borders",
            "gridlines",
            "resolution",
            "natural_earth",
            "ocean",
            "land",
            "lakes",
            "rivers",
        }
        features = {
            key: options.pop(key) for key in list(options) if key in feature_keys
        }
        features.setdefault("coastlines", True)
        bias_levels = options.pop("bias_levels", None)
        for i in range(self.axes.shape[0]):
            fields = [
                data.isel({self.row: i}) if self.row and self.row in data.dims else data
                for data in (self.observations, self.model, self.bias)
            ]
            fields = [data.where(np.isfinite(data)) for data in fields]
            if materialize == "row" and any(data.chunks is not None for data in fields):
                # Shared Dask dependencies are evaluated once per three-panel row.
                # This bounds temporary data to a row rather than persisting the cube.
                fields = dask.compute(*fields)
            for j, (subset, title) in enumerate(
                zip(fields, ("Observations", "Model", "Model − observations"))
            ):
                selected_norm = self.bias_norm if j == 2 else self.field_norm
                panel_options = dict(options)
                if self.kind == "contourf":
                    levels = (
                        bias_levels if j == 2 else panel_options.pop("levels", None)
                    )
                    if levels is None or np.isscalar(levels):
                        levels = np.linspace(
                            selected_norm.vmin,
                            selected_norm.vmax,
                            int(levels) if levels is not None else 11,
                        )
                    panel_options["levels"] = levels
                plotter = renderers[self.kind](
                    subset,
                    ax=self.axes[i, j],
                    data_crs=self.data_crs,
                    extent_crs=self.extent_crs,
                    lon_coord=self.x,
                    lat_coord=self.y,
                    style=self._style,
                    **features,
                )
                plotter.plot(
                    norm=selected_norm,
                    cmap=bias_cmap if j == 2 else cmap,
                    add_colorbar=False,
                    **panel_options,
                )
                self.plotters.append(plotter)
                self.mappables.append(plotter.mappable)
                ax = self.axes[i, j]
                if self.row:
                    title = f"{self.row} = {self.model[self.row].values[i]}\n{title}"
                ax.set_title(title)
                if panel_labels:
                    from ..api import _panel_letter

                    ax.text(
                        0.02,
                        0.98,
                        f"({_panel_letter(i * 3 + j)})",
                        transform=ax.transAxes,
                        va="top",
                        fontweight="bold",
                        bbox={"facecolor": "white", "alpha": 0.8, "edgecolor": "none"},
                    )
                if hasattr(plotter, "gridliner"):
                    grid = plotter.gridliner
                    if any(
                        (
                            grid.left_labels,
                            grid.right_labels,
                            grid.top_labels,
                            grid.bottom_labels,
                        )
                    ):
                        grid.top_labels = grid.right_labels = False
                        grid.left_labels = j == 0
                        grid.bottom_labels = i == self.axes.shape[0] - 1
        self.mappable = self.mappables[0]
        if colorbar:
            common = {"orientation": "horizontal", "pad": 0.08, **cbar_kwargs}
            self.colorbars.append(
                self.fig.colorbar(
                    self.mappables[0],
                    ax=list(self.axes[:, :2].flat),
                    **{"label": variable_label(self.model), **common},
                )
            )
            self.colorbars.append(
                self.fig.colorbar(
                    self.mappables[2],
                    ax=list(self.axes[:, 2].flat),
                    **{
                        "label": variable_label(self.bias),
                        **common,
                        **bias_cbar_kwargs,
                    },
                )
            )
        return self

docs.text:
Render with a common concentration scale and a zero-centered bias scale.

Explicit vmin/vmax and bias_limit avoid global scale reductions. With automatic limits, all required scalar reductions share one Dask compute call. bias_norm must be a TwoSlopeNorm centered on zero; explicit bias_limit uses symmetric bounds. Empty panels retain masked values.

Source code in src/monet_plots/plots/spatial_comparison.py 
def plot(
    self,
    *,
    vmin=None,
    vmax=None,
    norm=None,
    bias_limit=None,
    bias_norm=None,
    cmap="viridis",
    bias_cmap="RdBu_r",
    colorbar=True,
    cbar_kwargs=None,
    bias_cbar_kwargs=None,
    panel_labels=True,
    materialize="row",
    **kwargs,
):
    """Render with a common concentration scale and a zero-centered bias scale.

    Explicit vmin/vmax and bias_limit avoid global scale reductions. With
    automatic limits, all required scalar reductions share one Dask compute
    call. ``bias_norm`` must be a TwoSlopeNorm centered on zero; explicit
    ``bias_limit`` uses symmetric bounds. Empty panels retain masked values.
    """
    if self.mappables:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "This comparison has already been rendered; create a new plot to render again."
        )
    options = {**self.render_options, **kwargs}
    # Accept rendering configuration through the convenience constructor too.
    vmin, vmax = options.pop("vmin", vmin), options.pop("vmax", vmax)
    norm = options.pop("norm", norm)
    bias_limit = options.pop("bias_limit", bias_limit)
    bias_norm = options.pop("bias_norm", bias_norm)
    cmap, bias_cmap = options.pop("cmap", cmap), options.pop("bias_cmap", bias_cmap)
    colorbar = options.pop("colorbar", colorbar)
    cbar_kwargs = options.pop("cbar_kwargs", cbar_kwargs) or {}
    bias_cbar_kwargs = options.pop("bias_cbar_kwargs", bias_cbar_kwargs) or {}
    panel_labels = options.pop("panel_labels", panel_labels)
    materialize = options.pop("materialize", materialize)
    if materialize not in {"row", "panel"}:
        raise ValueError("materialize must be row or panel.")
    self.field_norm, self.bias_norm = _comparison_norms(
        self.observations,
        self.model,
        self.bias,
        vmin=vmin,
        vmax=vmax,
        norm=norm,
        bias_limit=bias_limit,
        bias_norm=bias_norm,
    )
    renderers = {
        "pcolormesh": SpatialMeshPlot,
        "imshow": SpatialImshowPlot,
        "contourf": SpatialContourPlot,
        "scatter": SpatialTrack,
    }
    feature_keys = {
        "extent",
        "coastlines",
        "states",
        "countries",
        "borders",
        "gridlines",
        "resolution",
        "natural_earth",
        "ocean",
        "land",
        "lakes",
        "rivers",
    }
    features = {
        key: options.pop(key) for key in list(options) if key in feature_keys
    }
    features.setdefault("coastlines", True)
    bias_levels = options.pop("bias_levels", None)
    for i in range(self.axes.shape[0]):
        fields = [
            data.isel({self.row: i}) if self.row and self.row in data.dims else data
            for data in (self.observations, self.model, self.bias)
        ]
        fields = [data.where(np.isfinite(data)) for data in fields]
        if materialize == "row" and any(data.chunks is not None for data in fields):
            # Shared Dask dependencies are evaluated once per three-panel row.
            # This bounds temporary data to a row rather than persisting the cube.
            fields = dask.compute(*fields)
        for j, (subset, title) in enumerate(
            zip(fields, ("Observations", "Model", "Model − observations"))
        ):
            selected_norm = self.bias_norm if j == 2 else self.field_norm
            panel_options = dict(options)
            if self.kind == "contourf":
                levels = (
                    bias_levels if j == 2 else panel_options.pop("levels", None)
                )
                if levels is None or np.isscalar(levels):
                    levels = np.linspace(
                        selected_norm.vmin,
                        selected_norm.vmax,
                        int(levels) if levels is not None else 11,
                    )
                panel_options["levels"] = levels
            plotter = renderers[self.kind](
                subset,
                ax=self.axes[i, j],
                data_crs=self.data_crs,
                extent_crs=self.extent_crs,
                lon_coord=self.x,
                lat_coord=self.y,
                style=self._style,
                **features,
            )
            plotter.plot(
                norm=selected_norm,
                cmap=bias_cmap if j == 2 else cmap,
                add_colorbar=False,
                **panel_options,
            )
            self.plotters.append(plotter)
            self.mappables.append(plotter.mappable)
            ax = self.axes[i, j]
            if self.row:
                title = f"{self.row} = {self.model[self.row].values[i]}\n{title}"
            ax.set_title(title)
            if panel_labels:
                from ..api import _panel_letter

                ax.text(
                    0.02,
                    0.98,
                    f"({_panel_letter(i * 3 + j)})",
                    transform=ax.transAxes,
                    va="top",
                    fontweight="bold",
                    bbox={"facecolor": "white", "alpha": 0.8, "edgecolor": "none"},
                )
            if hasattr(plotter, "gridliner"):
                grid = plotter.gridliner
                if any(
                    (
                        grid.left_labels,
                        grid.right_labels,
                        grid.top_labels,
                        grid.bottom_labels,
                    )
                ):
                    grid.top_labels = grid.right_labels = False
                    grid.left_labels = j == 0
                    grid.bottom_labels = i == self.axes.shape[0] - 1
    self.mappable = self.mappables[0]
    if colorbar:
        common = {"orientation": "horizontal", "pad": 0.08, **cbar_kwargs}
        self.colorbars.append(
            self.fig.colorbar(
                self.mappables[0],
                ax=list(self.axes[:, :2].flat),
                **{"label": variable_label(self.model), **common},
            )
        )
        self.colorbars.append(
            self.fig.colorbar(
                self.mappables[2],
                ax=list(self.axes[:, 2].flat),
                **{
                    "label": variable_label(self.bias),
                    **common,
                    **bias_cbar_kwargs,
                },
            )
        )
    return self

docs.title: Semantic versions and automatic releases
docs.text: MONET Plots uses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH versions. The package version lives in pyproject.toml; Release Please updates it together with .release-please-manifest.json and CHANGELOG.md in a release PR. monet_plots.__version__ reads installed package metadata, so it cannot drift from the built distribution.

docs.title: Everyday workflow
docs.text:
Use Conventional Commit titles for PRs and squash merge them into main. The PR title check enforces the syntax; configure squash merging to use the PR title as the commit message. If merging without squash, the actual commits must also follow the convention because Release Please reads commit history.

Commit or squash-merged PR title Version change fix(maps): correct raster extent Patch: 0.1.0 → 0.1.1 feat(maps): add spatial facets Minor: 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 feat!: change the plotting API Major: 0.1.0 → 1.0.0 Any supported type with BREAKING CHANGE: in its commit body Major docs: improve examples, test: cover facets, ci: update checks, chore: ... No release on their own

Breaking changes increment the major version even before 1.0.0. Mark corrections that change scientific interpretation as breaking when users must adapt their analysis. This automation produces stable releases; prerelease channels are not configured.

  1. Merge feature/fix PRs into main.
  2. After the complete CI matrix succeeds, Release Please opens or updates one release PR with the calculated version and release notes.
  3. Review and merge that release PR. Its normal CI checks validate the version files and the plotting library before it can be released.
  4. After CI succeeds on the merge commit, Release Please creates vX.Y.Z and a GitHub release. A reusable workflow builds a wheel and source archive from that tag, validates both archives' metadata, and attaches them to the release.

Do not manually bump version files or tag ordinary automated releases. The highest applicable bump wins when a release contains several changes. The bootstrap configuration starts from the current upstream commit and version 0.1.0; earlier repository history is excluded from the first generated changelog.

docs.title: One-time repository setup
docs.text:
A maintainer must configure these GitHub settings before automation can run:

  • Add the Actions secret RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN: a fine-grained token for a bot/maintainer with access to this repository and Contents: read/write and Pull requests: read/write. Follow organization token approval policies. Release Please uses it to open/update the release PR and create the release.
  • Allow GitHub Actions to create pull requests if repository/organization policy requires it. Enable squash merging with PR titles as squash commit messages.
  • Make the CI matrix and Conventional PR title / title checks required on main. Require review of release PRs as appropriate for the project.

A separate token is necessary because PRs created with the default GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger the normal pull_request CI workflows. Distribution uploads use the workflow's short-lived GITHUB_TOKEN, scoped to Contents: write; no PyPI password or API key is involved. Non-release jobs have read-only Contents permissions. Feature branches and fork PRs cannot run the release job.

This change only adds the configuration. It does not create credentials, alter remote repository settings, create a tag, or publish a release immediately.

docs.title: Recovering an interrupted artifact upload
docs.text: The tag and GitHub release are created before archives are uploaded. If packaging or uploading fails, fix the underlying problem and run Release distributions from the Actions tab with the existing tag (for example v0.2.0). The workflow validates package/manifest/tag versions and replaces the two archive assets on that release. GitHub Actions also retains the built archives as a workflow artifact. Do not move or reuse a published tag for a different commit.

docs.title: PyPI publishing
docs.text:
GitHub releases are automated now. PyPI publishing is not enabled because PyPI rejects direct URL dependencies, including the current Git-based monet-stats requirement. Before adding PyPI automation:

  1. Publish or identify an appropriate versioned monet-stats distribution and replace the Git requirement with that released dependency.
  2. Register the project on PyPI and configure a GitHub Actions trusted publisher for this repository and a dedicated publishing workflow/environment.
  3. Add an OIDC publishing job after the existing build and metadata checks.

Local checks can be run without any release credentials:

python scripts/check_release.py
python -m build
python scripts/check_release.py --tag v0.1.0 --dist-dir dist

Use the actual package version for the tag argument. There should be exactly one wheel and one source archive in dist/; remove stale local builds before checking a new version.

docs.title: Spatial maps and scientific comparisons
docs.text:
Use monet_plots.spatial for single maps and facets. The existing plot classes remain available. The default renderer is pcolormesh, supporting independent 1D coordinates and 2D curvilinear grids.

import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import monet_plots as mp

# ozone is an xarray.DataArray with dimensions model, season, lat, lon.
result = mp.spatial(
    ozone,
    row="model", col="season",
    projection=ccrs.LambertConformal(),
    data_crs=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
    extent=(-125, -65, 24, 51),
    cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=80,
    colorbar="shared", panel_labels=True,
    rasterized=True,
)
result.save("ozone-comparison.pdf")
result.save("ozone-comparison.png", dpi=300)

See the runnable model × season example. It includes seasonal station observations and a shared, horizontal colorbar.

docs.title: Coordinates and projections
docs.text:
projection is the display projection. data_crs describes the plotted coordinates; the default is geographic PlateCarree. Projected coordinates in metres require the corresponding Cartopy CRS. CF standard_name, degree units, and axis metadata are recognized before exact lon/lat, longitude/latitude, or x/y names. Ambiguous coordinates require explicit x= and y= overrides. Coordinate names alone never establish a projected CRS.

extent sets the viewport in extent_crs, which defaults to longitude/latitude, even when the plotted data is projected. imshow uses separate image_extent bounds in data coordinates. Otherwise regular coordinate centers determine its pixel edges. Irregular or curvilinear grids should use pcolormesh or contourf.

Descending independent grid axes are reordered together with their data. Station pairs and curvilinear coordinates retain their original pairing. Wrapped 1D longitudes are unwrapped without modifying the input. For a region crossing the dateline, use projection=ccrs.PlateCarree(central_longitude=180) and an extent in an appropriate extent_crs; a projection seam can split a map at its boundary. Both 0–360 and −180–180 longitude conventions can be plotted.

docs.title: Color scales and missing values
docs.text:
Facets use one normalization and one actual mappable colorbar by default. Use colorbar=False to retain comparable scales without a colorbar, or colorbar="each" to use independent panel scales. The legacy add_colorbar boolean remains supported by map_monet() and spatial plotters.

Explicit vmin/vmax, norm (including LogNorm and TwoSlopeNorm), colormap/norm tuples, and contour level sequences are supported. Supply either a norm or bounds. Contour colorbars reflect the actual contour levels, including unequal intervals. Missing values remain masked. Entirely missing datasets require explicit scale limits; individual empty panels work with the shared scale from other panels.

For a Dataset, select var_name="ozone" or facet with col="variable". Variables with different units require colorbar="each" or prior unit conversion. Matching unit strings do not establish scientific comparability: choose sensible variables and explicit scales for your scientific question. No automatic unit conversion, statistical aggregation, regridding, or significance inference occurs.

docs.title: Observations and customization
docs.text:
Pass observations=... and, for Dataset/DataFrame inputs, obs_var="ozone". Observations use each panel's normalization. Matching facet dimensions/columns are selected automatically; ungrouped points repeat across panels. obs_crs defaults to geographic coordinates independently of model coordinates. Known incompatible unit strings raise an error. Convert units explicitly before plotting.

The returned plot exposes fig, axes, artists, colorbars, save(), and close(). Spatial facet grids also expose plotters, mappables, and overlays. Customize them with ordinary Matplotlib. An existing Cartopy ax= can be supplied for a single map; it cannot be combined with facets.

from monet_plots import SpatialContourPlot

# Existing class constructors now remember their renderer during faceting.
comparison = SpatialContourPlot(ozone, row="model", col="season")
comparison.plot(cmap="viridis", levels=[0, 10, 20, 40, 80])

docs.title: Styles, performance and installation
docs.text:
Plot construction, rendering and saving apply their named style temporarily. Use mp.set_style("paper") for an intentional session-wide style, or with mp.style_context("paper"): for a temporary scope. Existing class return values remain unchanged; the convenience API returns the plot object.

Plot-owned xarray objects copy metadata without copying or computing their lazy arrays. Rendering computes only selected panels and, when necessary, global min/max reductions for a shared scale. Explicit bounds avoid those global reductions. Rasterize dense meshes in PDF/SVG output to keep file sizes manageable. Exact quantiles and unit conversion remain explicit preprocessing steps.

Python 3.11+ is required; CI exercises Python 3.11–3.14 on Linux, macOS and Windows. Static plotting needs the core dependencies; interactive plotting is available via pip install 'monet-plots[interactive]'. Development uses [test,docs]. The monet-stats Git dependency is pinned to an immutable commit for reproducible installs; replacing it with a versioned package release remains a packaging follow-up. Cartopy downloads Natural Earth features on first draw. Pre-cache these on offline systems or use coastlines=False and omit other downloaded map features.

def facet_time_map(
    da,
    time_dim="time",
    ncols=3,
    map_kws=None,
    projection=None,
    colorbar=True,
    figsize=None,
    cmap=None,
    vmin=None,
    vmax=None,
    norm=None,
    dpi=150,
    xlabel=None,
    ylabel=None,
    suptitle=None,
    cbar_label=None,
    xticks=None,
    yticks=None,
    annotations=None,
    export_path=None,
    export_formats=None,
    **kwargs,
):
    """
    Create a facet grid of map plots for each time slice in a DataArray using Cartopy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    da : xarray.DataArray
        The data to plot (must have a time dimension).
    time_dim : str, default: "time"
        Name of the time dimension.
    ncols : int, default: 3
        Number of columns in the facet grid.
    map_kws : dict, optional
        Dictionary of keyword arguments for map features.
    projection : cartopy.crs.Projection, optional
        Cartopy projection to use. Defaults to PlateCarree.
    colorbar : bool, default: True
        Whether to add a colorbar (shared).
    figsize : tuple, optional
        Figure size.
    cmap : str or Colormap, optional
        Colormap to use.
    vmin, vmax : float, optional
        Color limits.
    norm : Normalize, optional
        Matplotlib normalization.
    dpi : int, optional
        Dots per inch for export.
    xlabel, ylabel, suptitle : str, optional
        Axis labels and super title.
    cbar_label : str, optional
        Label for the colorbar.
    xticks, yticks : list, optional
        Custom tick locations.
    annotations : list of dict, optional
        List of annotation dicts for each subplot.
    export_path : str, optional
        Path to export the figure (without extension).
    export_formats : list, optional
        List of formats to export (e.g., ["png", "pdf"]).
    **kwargs : dict
        Additional keyword arguments for plotting.

    Returns
    -------
    fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
        The matplotlib figure object.
    axes : ndarray of matplotlib.axes.Axes
        The matplotlib axes objects.
    """
    # Setup
    projection = _setup_map_projection(projection)
    map_kws = map_kws or {}
    times = da[time_dim].values
    nt = len(times)

    # Create facet grid
    fig, axes, nrows, ncols = _setup_facet_grid(nt, ncols, projection, figsize, dpi)

    # Prepare plot arguments
    plot_args = dict(cmap=cmap, vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, norm=norm, add_colorbar=False)
    plot_args.update(kwargs)

    # Plot each time slice
    mesh = None
    for i, t in enumerate(times):
        ax = axes[i]
        dat = da.sel({time_dim: t})
        mesh = dat.plot(ax=ax, transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(), **plot_args)

        # Setup individual facet axis
        title = str(np.datetime_as_string(t))
        _setup_single_facet_axis(ax, map_kws, xlabel, ylabel, xticks, yticks, title)

        # Add annotations if provided
        if annotations and i < len(annotations):
            ax.annotate(**annotations[i])

    # Clean up unused axes
    for j in range(nt, len(axes)):
        fig.delaxes(axes[j])

    # Add shared colorbar
    _add_shared_colorbar(fig, axes, mesh, colorbar, cbar_label)

    # Set super title
    if suptitle:
        fig.suptitle(suptitle, fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")

    # Export figure
    _export_figure(fig, export_path, export_formats, dpi)

    return fig, axes

def plot_lines_map(
    df,
    lon_col="longitude",
    lat_col="latitude",
    group_col=None,
    projection=None,
    color="C0",
    linewidth=2,
    alpha=0.8,
    map_kws=None,
    figsize=(8, 6),
    dpi=150,
    title=None,
    export_path=None,
    export_formats=None,
    **kwargs,
):
    """
    Plot lines from a DataFrame on a Cartopy map. Optionally group by a column.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pandas.DataFrame or dask.dataframe.DataFrame
        DataFrame with longitude and latitude columns.
    lon_col, lat_col : str
        Column names for longitude and latitude.
    group_col : str, optional
        Column to group lines (e.g., for trajectories).
    projection : cartopy.crs.Projection, optional
        Cartopy projection to use. Defaults to PlateCarree.
    color : str or array-like, optional
        Line color.
    linewidth : float, optional
        Line width.
    alpha : float, optional
        Line transparency.
    map_kws : dict, optional
        Map feature keyword arguments.
    figsize : tuple, optional
        Figure size.
    dpi : int, optional
        Dots per inch for export.
    title : str, optional
        Plot title.
    export_path : str, optional
        Path to export the figure (without extension).
    export_formats : list, optional
        List of formats to export (e.g., ["png", "pdf"]).
    **kwargs : dict
        Additional keyword arguments for plt.plot.

    Returns
    -------
    fig, ax : matplotlib Figure and Axes
    """
    df = to_dataframe(df)
    # Setup
    projection = _setup_map_projection(projection)
    map_kws = map_kws or {}
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        subplot_kw={"projection": projection}, figsize=figsize, dpi=dpi
    )

    # Add map features
    _add_map_features(ax, map_kws)

    # Plot lines
    if group_col:
        for _, group in df.groupby(group_col):
            ax.plot(
                group[lon_col],
                group[lat_col],
                color=color,
                linewidth=linewidth,
                alpha=alpha,
                transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
                **kwargs,
            )
    else:
        ax.plot(
            df[lon_col],
            df[lat_col],
            color=color,
            linewidth=linewidth,
            alpha=alpha,
            transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
            **kwargs,
        )

    # Set title
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")

    # Finalize
    import warnings

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        fig.tight_layout()
    _export_figure(fig, export_path, export_formats, dpi)

    return fig, ax

def cmap_discretize(cmap, N):
    """Return a discrete colormap from a continuous colormap.

    Creates a new colormap by discretizing an existing continuous colormap
    into N distinct colors while preserving the color transitions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cmap : str or matplotlib.colors.Colormap
        Colormap instance or registered colormap name to discretize.
        Example: cm.jet, 'viridis', etc.
    N : int
        Number of discrete colors to use in the new colormap.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.colors.LinearSegmentedColormap
        A new colormap object with N discrete colors based on the input colormap.
        The name will be the original colormap name with "_N" appended.
    """
    if isinstance(cmap, str):
        cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
    colors_i = np.concatenate((np.linspace(0, 1.0, N), (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)))
    colors_rgba = cmap(colors_i)
    indices = np.linspace(0, 1.0, N + 1)
    cdict = {}
    for ki, key in enumerate(("red", "green", "blue")):
        cdict[key] = [
            (indices[i], colors_rgba[i - 1, ki], colors_rgba[i, ki])
            for i in range(N + 1)
        ]
    # Return colormap object.
    return mcolors.LinearSegmentedColormap(cmap.name + "_%d" % N, cdict, 1024)

def colorbar_index(
    ncolors,
    cmap,
    minval=None,
    maxval=None,
    dtype="int",
    basemap=None,
    ax=None,
    **kwargs,
):
    """Create a colorbar with discrete colors and custom tick labels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ncolors : int
        Number of discrete colors to use in the colorbar.
    cmap : str or matplotlib.colors.Colormap
        Colormap to discretize and use for the colorbar.
    minval : float, optional
        Minimum value for the colorbar tick labels. If None and maxval is None,
        tick labels will range from 0 to ncolors. If None and maxval is provided,
        tick labels will range from 0 to maxval.
    maxval : float, optional
        Maximum value for the colorbar tick labels. If None, tick labels
        will range from 0 or minval to ncolors.
    dtype : str or type, default "int"
        Data type for tick label values (e.g., "int", "float").
    basemap : matplotlib.mpl_toolkits.basemap.Basemap, optional
        Basemap instance to attach the colorbar to. If None, uses plt.colorbar.
    ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
        Axes to attach the colorbar to. If None, uses plt.gca().
    **kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments for plt.colorbar.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        (colorbar, discretized_cmap) where:
        - colorbar is the matplotlib.colorbar.Colorbar instance
        - discretized_cmap is the discretized colormap
    """
    import matplotlib.cm as cm

    cmap = cmap_discretize(cmap, ncolors)
    mappable = cm.ScalarMappable(cmap=cmap)
    mappable.set_array([])
    mappable.set_clim(-0.5, ncolors + 0.5)

    if basemap is not None:
        colorbar = basemap.colorbar(mappable, format="%g")
    elif ax is not None:
        from mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1.inset_locator import inset_axes

        # Use inset_axes to ensure the colorbar height matches the axes perfectly
        # regardless of aspect ratio or projection.
        cax = inset_axes(
            ax,
            width="5%",
            height="100%",
            loc="lower left",
            bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0),
            bbox_transform=ax.transAxes,
            borderpad=0,
        )
        cbar_kwargs = {"format": "%g", "cax": cax}
        cbar_kwargs.update(kwargs)
        colorbar = plt.colorbar(mappable, **cbar_kwargs)
    else:
        # Fallback for case where no axes is provided
        cbar_kwargs = {"format": "%g", "fraction": 0.046, "pad": 0.04}
        cbar_kwargs.update(kwargs)
        colorbar = plt.colorbar(mappable, **cbar_kwargs)

    colorbar.set_ticks(np.linspace(0, ncolors, ncolors))
    if (minval is None) & (maxval is not None):
        colorbar.set_ticklabels(
            np.around(np.linspace(0, maxval, ncolors).astype(dtype), 2)
        )
    elif (minval is None) & (maxval is None):
        colorbar.set_ticklabels(
            np.around(np.linspace(0, ncolors, ncolors).astype(dtype), 2)
        )
    else:
        colorbar.set_ticklabels(
            np.around(np.linspace(minval, maxval, ncolors).astype(dtype), 2)
        )

    return colorbar, cmap

def get_discrete_scale(
    data, cmap="viridis", n_levels=10, vmin=None, vmax=None, extend="both"
):
    """
    Get a discrete colormap and BoundaryNorm with 'nice' numbers.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : array-like
        The data to scale.
    cmap : str or matplotlib.colors.Colormap, optional
        The colormap to use, by default "viridis".
    n_levels : int, optional
        Target number of discrete levels, by default 10.
    vmin : float, optional
        Minimum value for the scale.
    vmax : float, optional
        Maximum value for the scale.
    extend : str, optional
        Whether to extend the scale ('neither', 'both', 'min', 'max'),
        by default "both".

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        (colormap, BoundaryNorm)
    """
    if vmin is None:
        vmin = np.nanmin(data)
    if vmax is None:
        vmax = np.nanmax(data)

    locator = MaxNLocator(nbins=n_levels, steps=[1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10])
    levels = locator.tick_values(vmin, vmax)

    if isinstance(cmap, str):
        cmap_obj = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
    else:
        cmap_obj = cmap

    n_colors = len(levels) - 1
    discrete_cmap = cmap_discretize(cmap_obj, n_colors)

    norm = mcolors.BoundaryNorm(levels, ncolors=discrete_cmap.N, extend=extend)

    return discrete_cmap, norm

def get_diverging_scale(data, cmap="RdBu_r", center=0, span=None, p_span=None):
    """
    Get a diverging colormap and normalization object centered at a value.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : array-like
        The data to scale.
    cmap : str or matplotlib.colors.Colormap, optional
        The colormap to use, by default "RdBu_r".
    center : float, optional
        The value to center the scale at, by default 0.
    span : float, optional
        The absolute range from the center (center +/- span).
    p_span : float, optional
        The percentile of absolute differences from center to use as span.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        (colormap, Normalize)
    """
    if span is not None:
        pass
    elif p_span is not None:
        diff = np.abs(data - center)
        span = np.nanpercentile(diff, p_span)
    else:
        span = np.nanmax(np.abs(data - center))

    vmin = center - span
    vmax = center + span

    norm = mcolors.Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
    if isinstance(cmap, str):
        cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)

    return cmap, norm

    data, cmap="viridis", vmin=None, vmax=None, p_min=None, p_max=None
):
    """
    Get a linear colormap and normalization object.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : array-like
        The data to scale.
    cmap : str or matplotlib.colors.Colormap, optional
        The colormap to use, by default "viridis".
    vmin : float, optional
        Minimum value for the scale. If None, uses min(data) or p_min.
    vmax : float, optional
        Maximum value for the scale. If None, uses max(data) or p_max.

    p_max : float, optional
        Percentile for maximum value (0-100).

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        (colormap, Normalize)
    """
    if p_min is not None:
        vmin = np.nanpercentile(data, p_min)
    if p_max is not None:
        vmax = np.nanpercentile(data, p_max)

    if vmin is None:
        vmin = np.nanmin(data)
    if vmax is None:
        vmax = np.nanmax(data)

    norm = mcolors.Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
    if isinstance(cmap, str):
        cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)

    return cmap, norm

def get_log_scale(data, cmap="viridis", vmin=None, vmax=None):
    """
    Get a logarithmic colormap and normalization object.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : array-like
        The data to scale.
    cmap : str or matplotlib.colors.Colormap, optional
        The colormap to use, by default "viridis".
    vmin : float, optional
        Minimum value for the scale (>0).
    vmax : float, optional
        Maximum value for the scale.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        (colormap, LogNorm)

    data_positive = data[data > 0]
    if vmin is None:
        vmin = np.nanmin(data_positive) if data_positive.size > 0 else 1e-1
    if vmax is None:
        vmax = np.nanmax(data)

    norm = mcolors.LogNorm(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
    if isinstance(cmap, str):
        cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)

    return cmap, norm

def compute(*objs: Any) -> Any:
    """Compute multiple lazy objects (xarray, dask, or cubed) simultaneously."""
    if not objs:
        return ()

    valid_objs = [obj for obj in objs if obj is not None]
    if not valid_objs:
        return objs if len(objs) > 1 else objs[0]

    # Check for Cubed
    try:
        import cubed

        if any(
            is_lazy(obj)
            and (
                isinstance(obj, cubed.Array)
                or (hasattr(obj, "data") and isinstance(obj.data, cubed.Array))
            )
            for obj in valid_objs
        ):
            res = cubed.compute(*objs)
            return res if len(objs) > 1 else res[0]
    except ImportError:
        pass

    # Check for Dask
    try:
        import dask

        if any(
            is_dask(obj)
            or (xr is not None and isinstance(obj, (xr.DataArray, xr.Dataset)))
            for obj in valid_objs
        ):
            res = dask.compute(*objs)
            return res if len(objs) > 1 else res[0]
    except ImportError:
        pass

    # Generic fallback
    results = []
    for obj in objs:
        if obj is not None and hasattr(obj, "compute"):
            results.append(obj.compute())
        else:
            results.append(obj)
    return tuple(results) if len(results) > 1 else results[0]

def get_plot_kwargs(cmap: Any = None, norm: Any = None, **kwargs: Any) -> dict:
    """
    Helper to prepare keyword arguments for plotting functions.

    This function handles cases where `cmap` might be a tuple of
    (colormap, norm) returned by the scaling tools in `colorbars.py`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cmap : Any, optional
        Colormap name, object, or (colormap, norm) tuple.
    norm : Any, optional
        Normalization object.
    **kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A dictionary of keyword arguments suitable for matplotlib plotting functions.
    """
    if isinstance(cmap, tuple) and len(cmap) == 2:
        kwargs["cmap"] = cmap[0]
        kwargs["norm"] = cmap[1]
    elif cmap is not None:
        kwargs["cmap"] = cmap

    if norm is not None:
        kwargs["norm"] = norm

    # If norm is present and not None, vmin and vmax should not be in kwargs
    # for many matplotlib functions (e.g., scatter, imshow).
    if kwargs.get("norm") is not None:
        kwargs.pop("vmin", None)
        kwargs.pop("vmax", None)

    return kwargs

def is_lazy(obj: Any) -> bool:
    """Check if an object is a lazy array (Dask or Cubed)."""
    if obj is None:
        return False
    if hasattr(obj, "chunks") and obj.chunks is not None:
        return True
    if (
        hasattr(obj, "data")
        and hasattr(obj.data, "chunks")
        and obj.data.chunks is not None
    ):
        return True
    return is_dask(obj) or is_cubed(obj)

def normalize_data(data: Any, prefer_xarray: bool = True) -> Any:
    """
    Normalize plot-owned data, copying metadata without computing lazy arrays.

    Args:
        data: Input data of various types
        prefer_xarray: Try xarray conversion for otherwise unrecognized data.
                      Existing xarray objects remain native and lazy. Native
                      Dask tables and arrays materialize as pandas DataFrames.

    Returns:
        Either an xarray DataArray, xarray Dataset, or pandas DataFrame
    """
    result = _normalize_data(data, prefer_xarray=prefer_xarray)
    if isinstance(result, (xr.DataArray, xr.Dataset)):
        return result.copy(deep=False)
    if isinstance(result, pd.DataFrame):
        return result.copy()
    return result

def to_dataframe(data: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Convert input data to a pandas DataFrame.

    Args:
        data: pandas DataFrame, xarray DataArray or Dataset, NumPy array,
              or a Dask DataFrame, Series, or array. Dask collections are
              computed here because the result is an in-memory table.

    Returns:
        A pandas DataFrame.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the input data type is not supported.
    """
    if isinstance(data, pd.DataFrame):
        return data

    if xr is not None and isinstance(data, (xr.DataArray, xr.Dataset)):
        return data.to_dataframe()

    if isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
        return _convert_array_to_dataframe(data)

    dask_table = _materialize_dask_table(data)
    if dask_table is not None:
        return dask_table

    if hasattr(data, "to_dataframe"):
        return data.to_dataframe()

    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported data type: {type(data).__name__}")

def validate_data_array(data: Any, required_dims: Optional[list] = None) -> None:
    """
    Validate data array parameters.

    Args:
        data: Data to validate
        required_dims: List of required dimension names

    Raises:
        TypeError: If data type is invalid
        ValueError: If data dimensions are invalid
    """
    if data is None:
        raise ValueError("data cannot be None")

    # Check if data has required attributes
    if not hasattr(data, "shape"):
        raise TypeError("data must have a shape attribute")

    if required_dims:
        if not hasattr(data, "dims"):
            raise TypeError("data must have dims attribute for dimension validation")

        for dim in required_dims:
            if dim not in data.dims:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"required dimension '{dim}' not found in data dimensions {data.dims}"
                )

def validate_dataframe(df: Any, required_columns: Optional[list] = None) -> None:

        required_columns: List of required column names

    if df is None:
        raise ValueError("DataFrame cannot be None")

    if not hasattr(df, "columns"):
        raise TypeError("object must have columns attribute")

    if required_columns:
        missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]

    if len(df) == 0:

class BasePlot:
    """Base class for all plots.

    Handles figure and axis creation, applies a consistent style,
    and provides a common interface for saving and closing plots.
    """

    def __init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs):
        """Keep styles local throughout construction, rendering and export."""
        super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)
        for name, method in list(cls.__dict__.items()):
            if callable(method) and (
                name == "__init__"
                or name.startswith("plot")
                or name
                in {
                    "save",
                    "add_features",
                    "map_monet",
                    "map_dataframe",
                    "add_map_features",
                }
            ):
                setattr(cls, name, _scoped_plot_method(method))

    @_scoped_plot_method
    def __init__(self, fig=None, ax=None, style: str | None = "wiley", **kwargs):
        """Initializes the plot with a consistent style.

        If `fig` and `ax` are not provided, a new figure and axes
        are created.

        Args:
            fig (matplotlib.figure.Figure, optional): Figure to plot on.
            ax (matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional): Axes to plot on.
            style (str, optional): Style name to apply (e.g., 'wiley', 'paper').
                If None, no style is applied. Defaults to 'wiley'.
            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for `plt.subplots`.
        """
        self._style = style
        self.mappable = None
        self.colorbars = []
        if ax is not None and fig is not None and ax.figure is not fig:
            raise ValueError("fig must be the figure that owns ax.")
        self._figure_style = FIGURE_STYLES.get(style)
        if style and self._figure_style is None:
            set_style(style)

        if ax is not None:
            self.ax = ax
            if fig is not None:
                self.fig = fig
            else:
                self.fig = ax.figure
        elif fig is not None:
            self.fig = fig
            self.ax = None
        else:
            with plt.rc_context(self._figure_style):
                self.fig, self.ax = plt.subplots(**kwargs)

        self.axes = np.asarray([[self.ax]], dtype=object)

    @property
    def artists(self):
        """Rendered scalar artists and any observation overlays."""
        primary = getattr(self, "mappables", None)
        if primary is None:
            primary = [] if self.mappable is None else [self.mappable]
        return [*primary, *getattr(self, "overlays", [])]

    @_scoped_plot_method
    @figure_style
    def save(self, filename, **kwargs):
        """Save the plot and wrap panel titles to their axes widths.

        Args:
            filename (str): The name of the file to save the plot to.
            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for `savefig`.
        """
        titles = [
            (ax, title, title.get_text())
            for ax in self.fig.axes
            for title in (ax._left_title, ax.title, ax._right_title)
            if title.get_visible() and title.get_text()
        ]
        if not titles:
            self.fig.savefig(filename, **kwargs)
            return
        # Resolve current layout and fixed-aspect axes before measuring.
        self.fig.draw_without_rendering()
        renderer = RendererAgg(1, 1, self.fig.dpi)
        original_sizes = [title.get_fontsize() for _, title, _ in titles]
        original_top = self.fig.subplotpars.top
        positions = None
        try:
            for ax, title, original in titles:
                wrapped = _wrap_title(title, ax.bbox.width * 0.98, renderer)
                if wrapped != original:
                    title.set_text(wrapped)
            bounded_export = (
                kwargs.get("bbox_inches", plt.rcParams["savefig.bbox"]) is None
            )
            if bounded_export and self.fig.get_layout_engine() is None:
                height = self.fig.bbox.height
                padding = renderer.points_to_pixels(2)
                top_limit = self.fig.bbox.y1 - padding
                excess = max(
                    title.get_window_extent(renderer).y1 - top_limit
                    for _, title, _ in titles
                )
                if excess > 0:
                    positions = [
                        (
                            ax,
                            ax.get_position(original=True).frozen(),
                            ax.get_in_layout(),
                        )
                        for ax in self.fig.axes
                    ]
                    min_top = self.fig.subplotpars.bottom + 0.12
                    self.fig.subplots_adjust(
                        top=max(min_top, original_top - excess / height)
                    )
                    self.fig.draw_without_rendering()
                    for ax, title, original in titles:
                        title.set_text(original)
                        title.set_text(
                            _wrap_title(title, ax.bbox.width * 0.98, renderer)
                        )
                        while (
                            title.get_window_extent(renderer).y1 > top_limit
                            and title.get_fontsize() > 1
                        ):
                            title.set_fontsize(title.get_fontsize() * 0.85)
                            title.set_text(original)
                            title.set_text(
                                _wrap_title(title, ax.bbox.width * 0.98, renderer)
                            )
            self.fig.savefig(filename, **kwargs)
        finally:
            if positions is not None:
                self.fig.subplots_adjust(top=original_top)
                for ax, position, in_layout in positions:
                    ax.set_position(position)
                    ax.set_in_layout(in_layout)
            for (_, title, original), size in zip(titles, original_sizes, strict=True):
                if title.get_text() != original:
                    title.set_text(original)
                if title.get_fontsize() != size:
                    title.set_fontsize(size)

    def close(self):
        """Closes the plot figure."""
        plt.close(self.fig)

    def add_logo(
        self,
        logo: str | Any | None = None,
        *,
        ax: matplotlib.axes.Axes | None = None,
        loc: str = "upper right",
        scale: float = 0.1,
        pad: float = 0.05,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Any:
        """Adds a logo to the plot.

        Parameters
        ----------
        logo : str or array-like, optional
            Path to the logo image, a URL, or a numpy array.
            If None, the default MONET logo is used.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            The axes to add the logo to. Defaults to `self.ax`.
        loc : str, optional
            Location of the logo ('upper right', 'upper left', 'lower right',
            'lower left', 'center'). Defaults to "upper right".
        scale : float, optional
            Scaling factor for the logo, by default 0.1.
        pad : float, optional
            Padding from the edge of the axes, by default 0.05.
        **kwargs : Any
            Additional keyword arguments passed to `AnnotationBbox`.

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.offsetbox.AnnotationBbox
            The added logo object.
        """
        import matplotlib.image as mpimg
        from matplotlib.offsetbox import AnnotationBbox, OffsetImage

        from ..plot_utils import get_logo_path

        if ax is None:
            ax = self.ax

        if logo is None:
            logo = get_logo_path()

        if isinstance(logo, str):
            if logo.startswith("http"):
                import io
                import urllib.request

                with urllib.request.urlopen(logo) as url:
                    f = io.BytesIO(url.read())
                img = mpimg.imread(f)
            else:
                img = mpimg.imread(logo)
        else:
            img = logo

        imagebox = OffsetImage(img, zoom=scale)
        imagebox.image.axes = ax

        loc_map = {
            "upper right": ((1 - pad, 1 - pad), (1, 1)),
            "upper left": ((pad, 1 - pad), (0, 1)),
            "lower right": ((1 - pad, pad), (1, 0)),
            "lower left": ((pad, pad), (0, 0)),
            "center": ((0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5)),
        }

        if loc in loc_map:
            xy, box_alignment = loc_map[loc]
        else:
            # If loc is not a string in loc_map, assume it might be a coordinate
            # tuple, but for simplicity we default to upper right if it's invalid
            if isinstance(loc, tuple) and len(loc) == 2:
                xy = loc
                box_alignment = (0.5, 0.5)
            else:
                xy, box_alignment = loc_map["upper right"]

        ab = AnnotationBbox(
            imagebox,
            xy,
            xycoords="axes fraction",
            box_alignment=box_alignment,
            pad=0,
            frameon=False,
            **kwargs,
        )

        ax.add_artist(ab)
        return ab

    def add_colorbar(
        self,
        mappable: matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable,
        *,
        ax: matplotlib.axes.Axes | None = None,
        label: str | None = None,
        loc: str = "right",
        size: str = "5%",
        pad: float = 0.05,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> matplotlib.colorbar.Colorbar:
        """Add a colorbar that matches the axes size.

        This method uses `inset_axes` to ensure the colorbar height (or width)
        matches the axes dimensions exactly, which is particularly useful for
        geospatial plots with fixed aspects.

        Parameters
        ----------
        mappable : matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable
            The mappable object (e.g., from imshow, scatter, contourf).
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            The axes to attach the colorbar to. Defaults to `self.ax`.
        label : str, optional
            Label for the colorbar, by default None.
        loc : str, optional
            Location of the colorbar ('right', 'left', 'top', 'bottom'),
            by default "right".
        size : str, optional
            Width (if vertical) or height (if horizontal) of the colorbar,
            as a percentage of the axes, by default "5%".
        pad : float, optional
            Padding between the axes and the colorbar, by default 0.05.
        **kwargs : Any
            Additional keyword arguments passed to `fig.colorbar`.

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.colorbar.Colorbar
            The created colorbar object.
        """
        from mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1.inset_locator import inset_axes

        if ax is None:
            ax = self.ax

        if loc not in {"right", "left", "top", "bottom"}:
            raise ValueError("loc must be right, left, top or bottom.")
        orientation = "vertical" if loc in ["right", "left"] else "horizontal"

        # Determine anchor and position based on location
        if loc == "right":
            bbox_to_anchor = (1.0 + pad, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)
            width, height = size, "100%"
        elif loc == "left":
            bbox_to_anchor = (-(float(size.strip("%")) / 100.0 + pad), 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)
            width, height = size, "100%"
        elif loc == "top":
            bbox_to_anchor = (0.0, 1.0 + pad, 1.0, 1.0)
            width, height = "100%", size
        else:  # bottom
            bbox_to_anchor = (0.0, -(float(size.strip("%")) / 100.0 + pad), 1.0, 1.0)
            width, height = "100%", size

        cax = inset_axes(
            ax,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            loc="lower left",
            bbox_to_anchor=bbox_to_anchor,
            bbox_transform=ax.transAxes,
            borderpad=0,
        )

        cb = self.fig.colorbar(mappable, cax=cax, orientation=orientation, **kwargs)

        if label:
            cb.set_label(label)
        self.colorbars.append(cb)
        return cb

@_scoped_plot_method
def __init__(self, fig=None, ax=None, style: str | None = "wiley", **kwargs):
    """Initializes the plot with a consistent style.

    If `fig` and `ax` are not provided, a new figure and axes
    are created.

    Args:
        fig (matplotlib.figure.Figure, optional): Figure to plot on.
        ax (matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional): Axes to plot on.
        style (str, optional): Style name to apply (e.g., 'wiley', 'paper').
            If None, no style is applied. Defaults to 'wiley'.
        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for `plt.subplots`.
    """
    self._style = style
    self.mappable = None
    self.colorbars = []
    if ax is not None and fig is not None and ax.figure is not fig:
        raise ValueError("fig must be the figure that owns ax.")
    self._figure_style = FIGURE_STYLES.get(style)
    if style and self._figure_style is None:
        set_style(style)

    if ax is not None:
        self.ax = ax
        if fig is not None:
            self.fig = fig
        else:
            self.fig = ax.figure
    elif fig is not None:
        self.fig = fig
        self.ax = None
    else:
        with plt.rc_context(self._figure_style):
            self.fig, self.ax = plt.subplots(**kwargs)

    self.axes = np.asarray([[self.ax]], dtype=object)

def __init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs):
    """Keep styles local throughout construction, rendering and export."""
    super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)
    for name, method in list(cls.__dict__.items()):
        if callable(method) and (
            name == "__init__"
            or name.startswith("plot")
            or name
            in {
                "save",
                "add_features",
                "map_monet",
                "map_dataframe",
                "add_map_features",
            }
        ):
            setattr(cls, name, _scoped_plot_method(method))

@_scoped_plot_method
@figure_style
def save(self, filename, **kwargs):
    """Save the plot and wrap panel titles to their axes widths.

    Args:
        filename (str): The name of the file to save the plot to.
        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for `savefig`.
    """
    titles = [
        (ax, title, title.get_text())
        for ax in self.fig.axes
        for title in (ax._left_title, ax.title, ax._right_title)
        if title.get_visible() and title.get_text()
    ]
    if not titles:
        self.fig.savefig(filename, **kwargs)
        return
    # Resolve current layout and fixed-aspect axes before measuring.
    self.fig.draw_without_rendering()
    renderer = RendererAgg(1, 1, self.fig.dpi)
    original_sizes = [title.get_fontsize() for _, title, _ in titles]
    original_top = self.fig.subplotpars.top
    positions = None
    try:
        for ax, title, original in titles:
            wrapped = _wrap_title(title, ax.bbox.width * 0.98, renderer)
            if wrapped != original:
                title.set_text(wrapped)
        bounded_export = (
            kwargs.get("bbox_inches", plt.rcParams["savefig.bbox"]) is None
        )
        if bounded_export and self.fig.get_layout_engine() is None:
            height = self.fig.bbox.height
            padding = renderer.points_to_pixels(2)
            top_limit = self.fig.bbox.y1 - padding
            excess = max(
                title.get_window_extent(renderer).y1 - top_limit
                for _, title, _ in titles
            )
            if excess > 0:
                positions = [
                    (
                        ax,
                        ax.get_position(original=True).frozen(),
                        ax.get_in_layout(),
                    )
                    for ax in self.fig.axes
                ]
                min_top = self.fig.subplotpars.bottom + 0.12
                self.fig.subplots_adjust(
                    top=max(min_top, original_top - excess / height)
                )
                self.fig.draw_without_rendering()
                for ax, title, original in titles:
                    title.set_text(original)
                    title.set_text(
                        _wrap_title(title, ax.bbox.width * 0.98, renderer)
                    )
                    while (
                        title.get_window_extent(renderer).y1 > top_limit
                        and title.get_fontsize() > 1
                    ):
                        title.set_fontsize(title.get_fontsize() * 0.85)
                        title.set_text(original)
                        title.set_text(
                            _wrap_title(title, ax.bbox.width * 0.98, renderer)
                        )
        self.fig.savefig(filename, **kwargs)
    finally:
        if positions is not None:
            self.fig.subplots_adjust(top=original_top)
            for ax, position, in_layout in positions:
                ax.set_position(position)
                ax.set_in_layout(in_layout)
        for (_, title, original), size in zip(titles, original_sizes, strict=True):
            if title.get_text() != original:
                title.set_text(original)
            if title.get_fontsize() != size:
                title.set_fontsize(size)
